body:
With `config_embed_metadata` on, `get_download_link` calls `do_kepubify_metadata_replace()`
(cps/helper.py ~1958 and ~2053) for every KEPUB download. That rewrites the entire epub zip
synchronously on the request greenlet — and under gevent without monkey.patch_all() that
freezes every other request for the duration.

Measured on a live instance with embed_metadata on (2026-08-05), downloading an 18.5 MB kepub
while sampling an unrelated `/login`:

    baseline            0.009 - 0.014 s
    during the download 1.026 s   (first sample; later samples back to ~0.010 s)
    download itself     1.292 s

So roughly a one-second whole-app stall per large KEPUB download. A Kobo taking twenty books
in a sync pays it twenty times.

This is pre-existing, but PR #1401 (prefer-KEPUB, default on) increases the share of downloads
that take this path, so the exposure grows. The fix shape is the same one used for the
conversion wait in #1401: keep the Flask-context work on the greenlet and hand only the zip
rewrite to `run_blocking` (cps/services/parallel.py:152). Note that Flask contextvars do not
cross that hop, so the offloaded callable must not touch url_for/gettext/session.
title: Every KEPUB download rewrites the whole zip on the request greenlet when embed_metadata is on
